The ivory used in this tool's handle is curious. Perhaps it was taken from one of the great beasts of the Abecean Sea?
A sealed horn inscribed with a prayer granting its holder luck.
Lurz gra-Shatul's odiferous ointment, applied to the neck, keeps a lot more than just vampires away.
A small metal rod with interchangeable and interlocking heads, designed to more easily craft unique maker's marks.
A rope of woven spidersilk on a hand-cranked brass wheel, marked with units of measurement, used to measure ocean depths.
A sturdy metal shovel, useful to any serious adventurer.
This small blue gem blinks softly in the proximity of poisonous, but odorless gases. Shatters if exposed to direct sunlight.
A whetstone etched with Nord symbology, used to grind and hone the edges of steel tools and implements.
An inexpensive but tasty wine bottled and sold at Ogondar's Winery, northeast of Belkarth.
Etchings depicting the fall of Orsinium cover this decorative hammer. "Never Forget" is emblazoned on the handle.
A pair of novelty oven mitts fasioned to look like cats' paws.
A small charm placed with valuable objects to repel thieves, burglars, robbers, and other criminal elements.
An expertly cut whetstone, given to students at the Rahni'Za sword school.
A complex recipe for an extremely pure and unusually strong form of skooma. A fence could sell this to many wealthy clients.
Only a mage could tell the difference between this and the authentic staff. A smuggler or con artist could find much use for it.
Sell to a merchant for gold.
If someone were to ride a senche-tiger, this is what they'd use.
Red silk backpack liner for care and transport of delicate lingerie, labeled 'Purple-Plumes' Bags, Anvil.'
A silver birdcall gifted to members of the Vinedusk Rangers by King Camoran, and used to send innocuous signals.
A small quartz wand. When touched to recently forged metal, the trip glows bright blue if the object is still too hot to hold.
Nets woven from the silk of giant spiders. Incredibly strong, but treated to remove the natural stickiness.
A pendant on a silver chain, worn to invoke the protection of Stendarr.
A very old, very valuable bottle of Summerset wine.
Amusing and often bawdy anecdotes and fables detailing a Breton's adventures in Alik'r.
Who would put makeup on a torchbug?
Talisman bearing the symbol of Arkay, said by the Keepers of the Ossuary of Telacar to repel the undead.
A once-ubiquitous iron pail used in the construction of Varen's Wall. The few that weren't melted down are collector's items.
A sweet-smelling oil, burned at night to make one's bedchamber calm and fragrant.
Malachite talisman carved to represent the Ring of Syrabane, said to increase the efficacy of spells, from the Eldritch Seal.
A relic from the first city built by Atmoran settlers in Skyrim, destroyed by the Snow Elves in the Merethic Era.
A set of sturdy drinking vessels carved from genuine sabre cat tusks and engraved with Breton symbology.
A finely-crafted wooden walking stick with a silver tip and a handle carved in the appearance of a sabre cat's head.
A small sack made of oiled sabre-cat skin, perfect for holding and organizing personal items.
In the hands of the right smith, these teeth are even better than nails.
Used by temples and monasteries across West Weald. Filled with wine from only Skingrad's finest vineyards.
Sacred Inkwell of Marukh the Seer
This finely crafted inkwell was likely used by the prophet Marukh during the days of the Alessian Order.
A pouch containing imitation seeds of a Hist tree, sold to gullible non-Argonians for their reputed fertile properties.
These long sharpened pins have hooked tips, used for unspeakable rites.
A large black dagger, ancient and dull, reputedly used to perform sacrifices to the great force of Sithis.
This lumpy cloth dolly has a split in the seam where its previous owner kept small secret treasures from parents and bullies.
This tablecloth was once a ship's jib sail--just the thing for semi-formal events in seaside taverns.
A short, somewhat desperate leaflet urging travelers and pilgrims alike to visit the Shrine of Saint Vorys in Sailenmora.
Jadeite statuette of a lissome dancer that gyrates when spun like a top, inscribed "Fuller's Break Ale" around the base.
A dark liquid layered artfully under the eyes to keep sailors from going blind while at sea.
The inside of the pillowcase is embroidered with lines of prayers and hidden desires to return home safely.
This porcelain model depicts the humble beadle kneeling in prayer to Julianos.
This silver chamber pot was made by the Knights of Saint Pelin as a gift for wealthy donors among Evermore's nobility.
This tapestry depicts the heroic sacrifice made by Saint Pelin when an army of vampires sieged Bangkorai Garrison.
This striking portrait of Saint Pelin is one of several that formerly lined the halls of Bangkorai Garrison.
Sisters who pledge themselves to the Order of Saint Pelin often wear these prayer shawls.
The Knights of Saint Pelin maintain a library of obscure historical scrolls at Bangkorai Garrison.
A common religious charm, this one is devoted to Saint Veloth, patron of outcasts and spiritual seekers.
A nutcracker in the shape of Saint Veloth, usually only used during Dark Elf holidays.
A small book of prayers gifted to the visitors to Saint Veloth's Shrine in exchange for voluntary contributions.
Preserved in a tooled leather case, this ancient prayer scroll was purportedly written by Saint Vorys the Immolant himself.
A provocative figurine of Meridia, Lady of Infinite Energies. Carved by an artisan with a vivid imagination.
Solstice Argonians spread this across their scales to retain moisture while sunning on the beach.
There isn't a Khajiit around who didn't own or know someone who owned their very own Sali the Senche-Lion doll.
A light cloth made from seaside plants, used to cover the head of the recently deceased during services.
Muck shovel with a solid Nord-forged blade, and coralwood haft with "Hrogar's Hold" burned into the wood.
A small kit with all the tools needed to mount and display a variety of saltwater dwellers. Plaque not included.
This small golden coffer contains a tiny molar. It is purported to be a preserved baby tooth of Emperor Reman II.
Players toss the handful of marbles and gems in this game into a sand garden, then take turns leaping to collect them.
An illustrated card depicting the Daedric Prince Sanguine offering the bearer a bottle.
A small pot of balm made from human blood, perfect for your next formal occasion.
Etched with Sanguine's rose. An inscription encourages owners to carry a little party with them wherever they go.
A doll modeled after an Argonian Sap-Speaker, albeit with a large head and smaller body, rarely seen this far from Murkmire.
Whether or not the sap comes from an actual Hist tree is hard to say, but it certainly sweetens any drink poured inside.
A small, but skillfully painted portrait of an Altmer Sapiarch. His expression suggests a lack of patience and high self-regard.
Used in some of the more time-sensitive trials at the knightly tourney held at Castle Navire.
A poster depicting the sigils of the three knightly orders that sponsor the Sapphire Tourney.
This pestle has a sapphire handle with a gold band. Dancing Khajiit are etched in the gold.
A lavishly decorated sack for carrying around books or other personal objects. It bears the symbol of the Daggerfall Covenant.
Satakalaam nobles anonymously place scintillating notes in each others' love pouches as part of a bizarre adult game.
This leather canteen is made from herbalist's satchels. Any drink remains fresh, though ultimately turns extremely bitter.
These delicate flowers were made by hand out of red satin. The long green stems look to be made of wood.
A luxury item from the Imperial City, this sleek wrap keeps hair hydrated and silky for fuss-free styling in the morning.
Savage Nord False Beard and Mustache
Comically hirsute false beard and mustache, worn when playing the "Strapping Skyrim Skald" game.
A string-operated puppet in the shape of a savage werewolf, now considered somewhat in bad taste due to events in Camlorn.
A full nested set of tightly woven bowls with lids that double as plates. Light as a feather and surprisingly sturdy.
Bones from various swamp creatures make up these false knuckles that protect the hand while crafting.
A small working model of a siege catapult. Miniature meatbags sold separately!
A thick brush used to rub off shedding scales. Not recommended for non-Argonian use.
Enchanted Scamp head mounted on a staff that squawks whenever a creature approaches the outskirts of a camp.
A ceramic bowl shaped like a smiling Scamp. A lid on its head opens to a hollow area for storing alchemical reagents.
A perfect, cleaned skull of a Scamp. Oddly heavier than one might expect.
A board game tray made from stretched and dried Scamp skin. Various unintelligible instructions are tattooed across the surface.
A collection of unseemly letters between two members of rivalrous noble families that would be embarrassing if brought to light.
A jar of vile-smelling goop. The label insists it can remove scars if applied daily, and liberally, for five consecutive years.
This kiln-fired platter had the irregular, wasteland grit of the Scar worked into clay, giving it an earthy, dappled appearance.
A pair of thin knives used by vampires to mark their preferred prey.
This lacy kerchief is dyed deep red - a convenient color for someone intent on hiding bloodstains.
This smooth paste reportedly maintains its vibrant red color throughout an entire feast.
A collection of miniature urns and offering plates. A comfort to many Dark Elves who are far from home.
A bottle of flowery perfume. The label promises to make anyone smell like a powerful magic-user.
Scent of Serenity Silvered Pill Tin
A pill tin bearing the mark of the Scent of Serenity alchemy shop in Riften, provided to its most exclusive customers.
When lit, the candle exudes the faintest scent of cardamom. A fence could resell it for certain necromantic rituals.
A scented pouch of something soft. Perfect for filling out anywhere one feels might be … lacking.
This thick black oil smells of woodsmoke and lavender. "The aromatic combination to drive Orcs wild!" claims the label.
A thick barb from a giant scorpion, modified with an eyelet to accommodate ropy thread.
A bowl made out of a repurposed claw-one that once belonged to a massive scorpion.
A double-bladed Wood Elf tool for peeling the carapace from a scorpion to get to the succulent meat inside.
A decorative pitcher made from a scorpion's shell, used to store and dispense milk produced by Wood Elf hogs.
A loud whistle fashioned from the shell of a dead scorpion.
This dried scorpion tail has been flattened to act as a bookmark.
Some Khajiit like to display their shed whiskers in cushions. This scorpion-shaped cushion has an iridescent metal base.
This scrawled bit of doggerel was written in the throes of a skooma trip. It is bad poetry. Really bad.
Multiple pieces of metal have been melted down to create this miniature likeness of Sotha Sil.
The trend of leaving vessels filled with polished scrap and scented oils about a dwelling is catching on in the Brass Fortress.
A magically enchanted femur, when chewed, produces hideous and creative illusory screams.
Part decoration, part security measure, this bird-like automaton emits a grating metal squeal when approached.
Popular among parents with children, these segments of scrib are dangled from stings and struck to produce soft, hollow notes.
A pan flute made from pieces of scrib chitin. When played, any scribs nearby perform a curious tapping-foot dance.
A segment of scrib antenna mounted to a wood frame that produces a whimsical sound when placed between the teeth and plucked.
A Dark Elf stone bowl and grinding tool, used to crush kwama scrib into a paste for cooking and alchemical preparations.
When filled with water, this small wooden whistle carved in the shape of a scrib makes a noise just like a scrib.
A racer-wing spoked hub driven by a small wheel and axle. Propels a cooling breeze and the aroma of rancid meat.
A torn sheet with dozens of scribbled and crossed-off ideas. The only legible note: "Werewolf Farm: endless wolf steaks."
An ornate dice casting cup carved from a single piece of whale bone.
The end of a carved mammoth's tusk serves as the perfect instrument to scrape mud off of one's boots.

param: A small [[Online:bird|bird]] wearing a crown--a common [[Lore:Systres|Systrean]] depiction of the [[Lore:Kynareth|{{sic|godess|goddess|nolink

value: Knife, pick, and chisel-this simple bronze tool is a versatile implement for carving bone, horn, and chitin.
Emblazoned with the symbol of Fargrave's Stricture, the liquid inside is pungent and foul.
This parchment, neatly rolled and tied with leather, keeps adventurers company during long, lonely nights on the road.
A polished metal bowl that's deep enough to hold water but shallow enough to see images of faraway places.
A delicately carved pipe, fashioned in the shape of one of the giant skeletons that looks over the city of Fargrave.
The thick crust of small metal bits cling to this powerful lodestone are easily shaped into simple designs for amusement.
A small hammer and set of chisels, used by stone sculptors to create statues, bas reliefs, and other carvings.
Most scholars dismiss tales of a massive turtle dwelling beyond the Weir Gate as pure nonsense … but this shell is really big.
This silver flask was given to every member of Captain Helane's crew before their maiden voyage. Only a few remain.
This finely tuned sextant bears the mark of the Sea Drakes and was likely owned by one of Captain Helane's midshipmen.
An assortment of sea-weathered glass beads and shards in a small wooden box.
A chunk of colored sea glass carved into the shape of a mudcrab and mounted to a small block for display.
A chunk of colored sea glass carved into the shape of a lion and mounted to a small block for display, just because.
A coral figurine skillfully crafted to resemble the terrifying Pyandonean sea monsters commanded by the Maormer.
This tongue-twisting tea set is enchanted to stay affixed to the tray, no matter how one's ship is tossed on the waves.
Sea Shell Full of Gold Teeth
Someone decided to store their unique collection in this natural container.
A string of barnacles polished to a sheen and set with perfect ocean pearls.
An enchanted net with grains of salt clinging to its fibers. Attracts and sticks to fish when thrown into shallow water.
Consisting of sand and finely crushed shells, this polish removes rust and other impurities caused by exposure to sea spray.
A wooden mold for making candles in the shape of a ship's bell.
A hand-sized portrait made of stained glass in the likeness of Kynareth. Hangable by a small chain.
Made from hardened seafoam, some Redguards use these to keep bugs from crawling into their ears while they sleep.
An empty redware jar that smells of mushrooms and peat. Used to preserve the Davon's Watch seasoning known as "seafood allspice."
This elaborate hairpin features seaglass arranged in gorgeous floral patterns. Perfect for seaside soirees.
This decanter is studded with rounded pieces of blue, green, and white glass that wash ashore.
Sailors who venerate Kynareth keepsake some seawater from their first successful voyage, a memento and lucky charm.
Someone's taken the time to gather seaweed, stone, and sticks to make this innovative dried-weed doll.
The wolf's head symbol of Haafingar Hold wrought in silver for display on a mantle.
A pressable wax seal carved in the shape of a flippered marine animal-like a smooth, tuskless horker.
A tightly stitched inflatable bladder. "Maiden's Breath" has been branded onto the side.
These thin paper napkins have been mildly enchanted to vaporize themselves and any dirt they've absorbed when crumpled.
A small pot of ink sealed with a faded sigil of the Empire, this was once used exclusively by bankers in Imperial City.
These Khajiit claws have grown sickeningly soft after many decades in the jar's pickled solution.
A partially-melted stick of red wax, used for sealing letters.
A well-made flat horsehair brush used by mariners to quickly and roughly clean themselves at sea.
A sturdy, hooped, wooden tankard. The handle seems to be made of a metal mooring cleat.
Hollowed by magic, this rock has been lovingly sanded smooth and produces a sound not unlike blowing over an empty bottle.
A lovingly polished stone that was engraved with all the laws of Clan Seamount. Use and age have rendered it illegible.
This dark green paint is thick and remarkably smooth. Perfect for decorating the craggy face of a Seamount warrior.
A coarse paste made from large chunks of salt. Good for cleaning out infection and drying wounds.
Nobility use the saltwater in this bottle when they style their hair in the elaborate up-dos currently in fashion on High Isle.
When Iron-In-Blood takes a break from crafting weapons, he makes these delicate chimes from local seashells.
Popular because it's easy to maintain, this net is laden with seashell weights.
A forger or a smuggler could make some coin selling these docking rights to Woodhearth's harbor.
The label claims the jar contains horse liniment, but a hidden internal label declares it "Proud Stallion Bedroom Ointment."
This map locates several hidden passes and caves that run through the mountains between Hallin's Stand and Satakalaam.
A cleverly designed pouch designed to be hidden within clothing so as to avoid the attention of pickpockets.
The glass bulbs of this hourglass are encased in a gold stand. The sand within is a grayish white and measures a minute's time.
This budding seed bristles with new growth, ready for a young Bright-Throat to practice the art of trimming it.
This black meditation stone has been molded by the Primeval Seekers into a likeness of Hermaeus Mora.
Attached to the end of a fishing line, this appendage grabs fish rather than hooks them. Just be sure it doesn't grab you.
The bits on this ornamental onyx key are jagged, long, and irregular.
One of ten thousand pieces of the cloth mosaic that adorned the halls of the Dwemer king. Supposedly awe inspiring when whole.
This votive glass sphere clocks worship hours by channeling sand through unseen tunnels that form elaborate geometric patterns.
This tiny curiosity resembles a dreugh and moves about when exposed to water. Some surmise it came from the Clockwork City.
This small booklet contains shortened and simplified versions of Sotha Sil's Sermons.
These grotesquely exaggerated metal jaws may be wound to chew according to prescribed mastication settings for several minutes.
This feeder siphons incentivizing treats for Scamps in order to alter their behavior.
Once the sand fills the bottom chamber, this hourglass automatically reverses itself and starts the timer again.
This blacksmithing vise grips and loosens objects at the press of a pedal.
A handful of flawed beryls, aquamarines, and chalcedonies marked with ancestral runes, made into coat buttons.
The skin of a senche-tiger with a sewn-in silk lining, used as a bedroll in the wilderness.
The head of this beautifully carved ink brush is composed of hundreds of genuine Senche whiskers.
Made from shed Senche whiskers, this coarsely bristled brush is prized by Senche riders for grooming their mounts.
A hairbrush made from the jawbone of a senche-tiger.
The golden fur lining this blanket contrasts beautifully against its red fabric.
For the discerning warrior who wants to add a bit of flair to his or her wardrobe.
This fancy luggage item is made from the skin of a senche-tiger. The tiger's claws and teeth are used as fasteners.
A pair of earplugs which hiss softly when senche-tigers approach within thirty paces. Indispensable for light outdoor sleepers.
Drinking from this gilded bowl is considered strictly taboo for Cathay, Dagi, and other thumbed bipeds.
Scholarly Senche-raht place this thin wooden implement between their teeth and use its long stem to navigate their books.
A training harness, only slightly gnawed.
Pricier than standard twine and subject to social disapproval, the intestines of senche-tigers make for stout fishing line.
Some followers of Mora cover both eyes and ears with this mask, ensuring they can better perceive their lord's whispers.
A set of expertly crafted Redguard cutlery, imported from Alik'r for use only by the most discerning chefs.
A badge carried by high-ranking officers of the Sentinel Guard.
This document contains details about patrol routes and shift schedules for the Sentinel Guard.
This small hand mirror was made so the Sentinel Guard can communicate across long distances.
A Redguard medal bearing the image of a lion on the front and a Sentinel maker's mark on the back.
Imported from Alik'r, this cerulean-clay cup is designed to be spill-proof for the use of young children.
A silver barb-lined strap to dig into the wearer's chest, held in a small box. They are used by members of a secret cult of Sep.
The seriweed grows only in Black Marsh and is extremely rare. Its distilled sap is a potent cure for many kinds of poison.
A container of slitted metal balls affixable to fishing line. Ideal for weighing down lines to catch bottom feeders.
Serpent's Tongue is a striking wildflower of Black Marsh. This lace doily captures the delicate shape of its blooms and vines.
Tattered silk embroidered with Maormer runes of rulership and bearing the entwined image of mating sea serpents.
Used to rapidly produce small daggers for Tide-Born hunters. The serrated edge helps crack through crab or Hadolid shell.
This mechanized brace not only supports an injured or infirm limb, but also lends the strength of a slightly less frail person.
These dice are quite heavy. The gleaming brass offsets the dots carved on each side.
A set of four soft deer-chamois hand-cloths, stamped on the corners, "Riverside Inn, Nimalten."
A set of four fine deer-chamois handtowels, stamped on the corners "Trader's Rest, Velyn Harbor."
An assortment of chisels fit to cover most hewing needs.
Set of six crystal shot glasses engraved with an image of the Overlook Inn.
Made of cork oak bark and coated to provide a tight seal and a smooth opening.
Four fine glass goblets with gilt brims, imported from Gilane in southern Hammerfell.
Four star-shaped enameled ceramic ramekins for poaching bantam guar eggs, from the Southpoint Inn.
Set of six greenglass mazte glasses with gilded brims, from the Hissing Guar Cornerclub in Kragenmoor.
Set of Kwama Scrib Dining Spikes
Six quartz-handled spikes. Good for impaling kwama scribs to wooden plates so they may be eaten alive-as is tradition.
Set of Mineral-Based Paints of Rare Colors
Sectioned shellmold box containing eight bottles of bright mineral-based paints in rare colors, quite valuable.
Case of six fine tweezer utensils used for eating live bugs, carved from flexible monkeybone and inscribed "Silvenar Supplies."
Set of six heirloom silver-plated marrow spoons, each stamped with the Great Seal of Silvenar in its bowl.
Set of fancy frog-kabob skewers of twisted wrought iron, from the Greenwarden Forge in Elden Root.
Set of Snow Ogre Nail Spoons
Splendid gift set of eight gilt spoons with scrimshaw handles, the bowls crafted from snow ogre fingernails.
Set of seven cut-glass jigger cups, used for sipping fermented syrups, from the Vitriarch at Cat's Eye Quay.
Set of four shot glasses etched with the crest of House Tamrith.
Seven different pairs of finely-wrought golden bells, one for each week day, for attaching to curly-toed slippers.
Seven superb tail-bows, each in the traditional color associated with a day of the week.
Small flute that can be played seventeen different ways to imitate and attract every species of songbird native to Auridon.
These steel-plated horseshoes were forged by Imperial smiths for members of the Seventh Legion.
This lantern is forged from Dwarven Steel and engraved with the words: "For your loyalty to the Empire, from Septima Tharn."
This elegant sash is handed out to Imperial agents so that when the legion arrives, they can prove their loyalty.
This silver trowel is used by Imperial archaeologists working as part of the Seventh Legion.
A pin given to students who complete their studies at the Shad Astula Academy of Magic.
Collection of eight sealed glass jars, each containing a sample of mud from a different region of Shadowfen.
Trifles and Ornaments, Dishes and Cookware
A brass medallion inscribed with the likeness of Sithis, the Dread Father, used to identify fellow members of the Shadowscales.
This padded mat made from soft void cloth is used primarily by mourners in Necrom.
A small glass phial with curled, yellowed nail clippings inside. Label reads "Archmagus Shalidor."
Tattoo ink obtained by milking bloated shalks. Slightly more blue than common tattoo ink.
The barbed mandibles of a giant beetle, shaped into a pair of painful bindings. Pulling free would leave deep wounds.
A lidded heavy pan used to slow-roast shalks. It can be used as a serving vessel as well.
A small device made of hardened shalk resin, designed to keep a Dark Elf's nails neat and trim.
A sundial made of shalk resin, small enough to sit on a windowsill, used to track cooking times in complex Dunmeri recipes.
Fashioned to sift through the dark swamp mud for small treasures such as eggs, bugs, and animal bones.
A pillowcase of fine linen embroidered with prayers invoking Saint the Wise to grant nights of deep, restful sleep.

Believed to be a blessed instrument of Z'en, the Kothringi christened many endeavors by breaking ground with this shovel. NOTE: This item is on Kari's Hit List! Bring it to the Thieves Den and place it in the library to prove you're a Master Thief.
A small hand ax meant for planing down a log or block of wood before applying more precise tools.
This sliver of crystal buzzes angrily, releasing intermittent pulses of purple light. It may be a fragment of an Ideal Master.
Large pieces of black onyx, carried by priests of Sithis for various meditation practices.
A woman's necklace made from polished shark teeth.
Apothecary implements used to prepare ingredients by crushing or grinding them into paste or powder.
The druids weave three-sided knots into the pattern of this shawl.
This piece of shattered black metal seems to drink light. Part of an emblazoned Daedric script runs along its length.
The specially shaped stone within this soft leather sheath allows Khajiit to file, shape, and help shed their claws.
A wooden dowel wrapped in hefty rope usually kept near a vanity for Khajiiti claw care.
A complete set of unused echatere paint in the distinctive color palette of Shatul clan.
Each piece of parchment is unstained, unmarred, and unfolded.
Rope woven from sheep's gut, extra strong.
A travel-sized and much less rowdy version of the Nord drinking game, made popular at the Sober Nord Inn.
Sheepskin covers this porcelain jug to keep its contents from spoiling.
Contains sheet music for such classics as "Lusty Argonian Maid" and "No Way Am I Going to Eat this Stew."
This black-sand timer has Sheggorath's name in tiny letters all over it in swirls. It does not measure time consistently.
One of a series of small worrystones made by an artisan that witnessed Sai Sahan summon his own spirit sword.
A soldier's first aid kit containing various bandages, curatives, and scale liniment in a handy shoulder bag.
Polished to a smooth shine, this piece of Shellbug Chitin could be used to hold jewelry or coins.
A small, flat reed mat with several strange markings upon it. Used in the game shells and stones.
A fine piece of cloth made for Argonians to clean between their scales.
A blend of coconut oil, sea salt, and ground pumice stone brings a nice shine to any smile.
A specialized deck of cards used to play the Dark Elf game known as "Shenanigans."
Magnifying lens of imported Shimmerene glass in a brass setting with a carved tigerbone handle.
A large, beautifully painted vase used to store oil for ceremonies. A craftmans stamp reveals its origins to be Shimmerene.
High Elf cuisiniers use this long, curved implement to pry delicious snails from their shells.
This ammonite emits a faint glow on account of its untapped arcane energies.
A mounted knight with metal sword, shield, and armor. It does not bear the livery of any particular house.
A lightweight piece of shiny copper, cut to attract a fish's eye in murky water.
A finely-crafted model of the Abecean Monarch, an Altmer ship of the All Flags Navy, constructed inside a small-necked bottle.
A finely-woven cargo net folded inside a canvas bag, apparently never used.
A ship's sextant made of polished brass.
A brass-and-glass ship's lantern fitted with a set of hinged shutters, used for ship-to-ship communication at sea.
The alchemical liquid inside this circular carpentry tool is enchanted to glow when aligned on a level surface.
A detailed shipwreck model bafflingly constructed inside a glass bottle with a tiny neck.
A fine silken bedcover supposedly given to Admiral Bendu Olo the night the All Flags Naval Base finished construction.
A hard, chalky substance purported to treat the effects of skooma sickness. Chew twice daily for best effects.
A collection of Shor's Stones tokens, obviously important to their owner, such as gaudy cloth patches and other nostalgic items.
Strapped onto boots, these attachments have lateral wings that distribute the weight and make it easier to cross tidal pools.
A scrawled paper listing wines and ales enjoyed or not. It almost reads as if the person writing this was drunk.
A saddle bearing the mark of the once-famous Shornhelm Cavalry that used to patrol the Rivenspire roads.
An ornate and rather ostentatious drinking vessel awarded to officers in good standing with the Shornhelm Guard.
A pair of tickets for the annual performance of the play, "Ranser! You Madman!" at the Dead Wolf Inn.
An official stamp used by the Triumvirate of Shornhelm. A forger would pay much for this.
Expensive parchment embossed with the Seal of Shornhelm and used by the ruling Triumvirate for official correspondence.
One of the crystal jars Baron Dorell filled for every swear word he let slip during public sessions. Sadly, this one is empty.
Trifles and Ornaments, Dishes and Cookware
A pair of carved wooden wedges designed to be inserted into shoes, subtly increasing the wearer's apparent height.
It's impossible to tell what kind of clothing this article once was, but the cloth may be salvaged into a fetching kerchief.
These simple cotton pants are ripped to shreds, seemingly from powerful legs tearing through the fabric.
Fancy jar-top opener that uses the open-mouthed skull of a giant shrew, labeled "Courtesy of Beleth's Swamp Food."
Pieces of fish bones are stuck to this picnic cloth. What the tide giveth it also takes back, as the Tide-Born saying goes.
The dried mushroom stem planks of this tackle box are remarkably light and buoyant. Edible too, if the fish aren't biting.
The grisly paw of a large cat, or possibly a Khajiit, kept with belongings as a ward against burglars.
An ancient, shrunken head of a Hagraven, thought by Reachmen to be a powerful talisman of good luck.
This shriveled, mummified head of a monkey is intended to be a charm to ward off evil swamp spirits.
Despite having the skull removed, this head is still the size of a normal adult wolf and has Reach glyphs painted all over it.
This sun dial serves two purposes: it tells time but also doubles as a heliograph to send messages across the battlefield.
These blank documents bearing the coat of arms of a noble house and signed by a house officer would be worth a lot to a forger.
A wooden cudgel used in the violent sport Gulob. Supposedly signed by the late One-Tooth Skrib, but likely a forgery.
These blank heraldic documents are signed by Thane Unnvald of Riften. They would be worth a small fortune to a forger.

* This ability now provides the buff Major Fortitude. * Green Dragon Blood: This ability now provides the buffs Major Fortitude and Major Endurance, and lasts for 23 seconds at the maximum rank. * Coagulating Blood: This ability now provides the buffs Major Fortitude and Minor Vitality, and lasts for 23 seconds at the maximum rank.
* Restoring Aura: This ability no longer removes major buffs from allies, such as Major Fortitude granted by Green Dragon Blood.

* This ability and its morphs can now Critically Strike. **Developer Comment: The goal of this change was to bring Dragon Blood in line with other heal abilities in the game. * Coagulating Blood: ** This morph now heals for a flat value (scaling with Spell Damage and Max Magicka), with that heal being increased by up to 33% based on your missing health. ** This morph no longer grants the Minor Vitality buff. ***Developer Comment: We wanted to give Dragonknights a more reliable version of Dragon Blood that scaled like other heal abilities in the game. However, it was still important to us that it retained some of the risk/reward of waiting to use it at lower health thresholds. Because there's a base heal value, it's more forgiving when used at higher health, but waiting makes it more efficient. To counterbalance this increased ease of use, we moved the Minor Vitality buff to Green Dragon Blood. This also ensures that Health-based Dragonknights also have a strong morph option as well. * Green Dragon Blood: This morph now grants the Minor Vitality buff as well as Minor Endurance.
* Coagulating Blood: Increased the heal of this morph by approximately 19% to put it better in line with other burst heal abilities.

* Coagulating Dragon Blood (morph): Increased the base healing of this ability by approximately 12% to ensure it's closer in line with other heals, such as Breath of Life. With this new value, the heal for Coagulating should be slightly weaker than these heals (Breath of Life, Blood Sacrifice, etc.) while above 50% Health, but slightly stronger than them while below 50% Health. The deviation in healing effectiveness will be between 0 and 16.5%.

* Coagulating Blood (morph): ** Fixed an issue where this ability appeared to rank up in 1 second duration per rank. ** Reduced the cost of this ability to 3780, down from 4320, to add an improvement to the morph rather than just changing its functionality.

* Coagulating Blood (morph): ** This morph no longer reduces in cost, but instead increases the healing bonus based on your missing Health to 50%, up from 33%. ** The healing bonus is now a true value, rather than an additive value. ** Reduced the base healing of the skill by approximately 3% to fix some calculation errors. **Developer Comment: This skill is currently enabling the Dragonknight to bounce back from near death situations a little too frequently, where its significant cost reduction compared to other burst heals of its nature is allowing it to be cast with reckless abandon. By taking away the cost reduction bonus on the morph, we needed to find another morph empowerment to ensure the skill felt like it was gaining something, rather than changing something. As the skill IS meant to bring you back from Death's Door, we wanted to reinforce this with the execute scaling increase, but hopefully we see the frequency of returning from the brink a little less frequently.

* Green Dragon Blood (morph): ** This morph now also adds a small Heal over Time, lasting 5 seconds and scaling off your Max Health (~3% per tick). ** This morph no longer increases in duration of effects by 1 second for every rank, but rather ranks up the healing done of the healing over time. *** We're seeing many tanks opt to take Coagulating Blood over Green Dragon Blood in organized groups, where buffs bring up their offensive stats enough to eclipse the healing potential of Green Dragon Blood. To help mitigate this, we're adding a small guaranteed heal that uses your Max Health to offer some diverging game play options, rather than bloating out the Missing Health values of GDB and creating different problems out of that.

The residual Health cost also lasts 1 second less causing it to drain less Health, to ensure its total cost is reduced to the expected level. **Developer Comment: For a long time, these abilities have had relatively low engagement due to the fact that they costed purely Health and hurt the user more the higher their stats were, making it both deadly and un-advantageous to run in situations where you needed to stay alive. In addition, the health cost had low interplay with mechanics - such as cost reduction - and made it difficult to play around, leaving its core concept unsatisfying and untapped. We've decided to switch this ability over to a Dual Cost skill with the brunt of its cost being on the Magicka side of things, and the rest of it filled in with Health (it equals the base 4590 burst heal cost that skills such as Rushed Ceremony have when you add them up!). In addition, we've allowed the heal to be self-targetable so the healer can keep themselves up in a situation of need and giving the class a much-needed reactive self-heal. Overall, we hope this helps the skill stand out as something unique and thematic to the class, with less overall restrictions and punishment on the caster.

This rework has not adjusted how the invisibility functionality removes itself, and casting certain abilities will continue to naturally disable the effect (and penalties) the same as before. ** Developer Comment: In this pass we're looking at the opportunity costs of Shadow Cloak and trying to create a more accessible skill for any Nightblade build, while simultaneously ensuring there are more stark costs associated with maintaining invisibility. The toggled nature should make the activation of Shadow Cloak feel significantly smoother to weave in and out of the shadows, while the disabling of Magicka Recovery while moving should stomp out the ability to perpetually remain undetected without serious investment and strategic use. In addition to this, we're adding a small benefit for activating the skill in PvE situations, where the invisibility often outright doesn't work or incurs a heavy DPS loss. The goal with Born from Shadow is not to outright carry damage in PvE, but rather give us a foundation to potentially build off of by allowing us to easier track when Nightblades utilize the sneaky parts of their toolkit in future iterative work.

Simultaneously, this will let us re-evaluate other parts of the Nightblade kit in the future, to find healthier spots to bring them up in PvE damage production without further complicating some of their PvP strengths.

* Improving the Werewolf gameplay and quality of life: Several abilities received significant adjustments, leveling the skill line is considerably easier, and Werewolves are now capable of doing more core combat actions such as resurrecting or using synergies. * Developer Comments - Werewolf Changes: There were a significant number of changes made to Werewolf this update. Some of these changes were made to improve the quality of life with leveling and maintaining the form, while others open up new gameplay possibilities.: First, you'll find leveling and maintaining your Werewolf is now considerably easier. The Devour passive is now granted automatically from the very start, so you can sustain the form better at lower levels before you've unlocked all the other skills. We've also significantly reduced the experience requirements to morph all skills.: Second, you'll be able to do more core combat actions as a Werewolf, such as resurrecting your allies or using Synergies. Werewolves will have a much easier time engaging in group content now that they can help their friends more effectively. This, coupled with some other changes such as the Blood Rage passive triggering on damage dealt instead of damage taken, means they can be more viable in group PvE activities such as dungeons.: Finally, many morphs and abilities were changed to improve the cohesiveness of the Werewolf kit. Some combos and effects that weren't very effective have been removed, while others were tweaked to better support the fast and ferocious playstyle of the Werewolf. As an example, we removed the stuns from Pounce and Piercing Howl, but dramatically improved Roar by making it instant cast, fear more targets, and have more competitive morph effects. * Werewolf Transformation: ** You can now resurrect other players while transformed. ** You can now use synergy abilities while transformed. * Werewolf Bleed: Adjusted this ability and its morphs to follow our standardized Damage over Time ruleset. ** Total duration decreased to 4 seconds from 8 seconds. ** Added a 1 second delay between the initial hit and the first tick. ** Decreased the damage per tick by approximately 15% for the base and Pack Leader morph. ** Increased the damage per tick by approximately 24% for the Berserker morph. ** These abilities can no longer refresh once they are applied to a target. *** Developer Comment: Previously, a big portion of Werewolf's burst damage came from the fact that their bleed applied from their Light Attacks dealt damage immediately, and could be spammed in quick succession. This made up for the fact that immediately Light Attacking would refresh the bleed. Now with the delay, we wanted to ensure you couldn't miss the damage, so we're making sure these bleeds couldn't refresh if they were already active. In addition to this, we've noticed a large disparity of the performance between the Pack Leader and Berserker morph, and are currently in the midst of investigating a healthier balance between the two, other than merely adding more damage to one.

* Reduced the damage dealt by your Light and Heavy Attacks with this ability and its morphs by approximately 17%. * Increased the range of the Light Attacks to 7 meters from 5 meters, and the Heavy Attacks to 10 meters from 7 meters. This was done to help preserve the same distance from standard forms, since your character size increase was not applying to the range of your abilities, causing your attacks to appear as if they lost range. * This ability and the Pack Leader morph no longer apply a bleed to enemies hit with Light Attacks, or deal area damage with Heavy Attacks. * Pack Leader: ** The Direwolves can no longer be targeted or die. ** Reduced the damage of the Direwolves' Gnash attack by approximately 70%, and decreased the frequency of its attack speed to 2 seconds from 1 second. ** Gnash now applies Minor Maim to enemies hit for 4 seconds. ** Reduced the damage of the Lunge attack by approximately 60%. ** Lunge will now be cast every 10 seconds, rather than have a 25% chance every 3 seconds to cast. ** Lunge will now snare enemies hit by 30% for 4 seconds. ** The Direwolves will now return to your side if you travel far enough away from them, since they are lost and confused without their leader of the pack. * Werewolf Berserker: Increased the damage of the bleed from your Light Attacks by 25%. ** Developer Comment: The werewolf morphs were initially designed to have Pack Leader emphasized on utility, while Berserker was meant to be the offensive and raw damage choice. Due to the Direwolves' damage and attack speed, Berserker was constantly eclipsed, and Pack Leader wasn't provided much utility other than causing target complications for enemies. Now, Pack Leader allows your doggos to enfeeble your foes, while Berserker lets you rip and tear.
